questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

A few minutes later a request came that all members of the house party should __assemble__ in the drawing-room.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option(2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"assemble"** means to gather together in one place for a common purpose. (एकत्रित करना)

 
 
• **Example: **The students were asked to assemble in the auditorium for the event.
 
 
 
• **"Disperse"** refers to breaking apart and going in different directions; to spread widely. (बिखेरना, तितर-बितर होना)
 
 
• **Example: **The crowd began to disperse after the concert ended.
 
 

Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'assemble'** is **'disperse'**.

• **Gather** (इकट्ठा करना): To come together into one place or group.

 
 
• **Example: **The family will gather for the annual reunion.
 
 
 
• **Search** (तलाश करना): To look for something carefully.
 
 
• **Example:** They had to search the entire area for the missing keys.
 
 
 
• **Guard** (रक्षा करना): To protect someone or something from danger or harm.
 
 
• **Example:** The soldiers guard the borders day and night.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

We love Nathan.

options.text: Nathan is being loved by us.
Nathan has been loved by us.
Nathan have been loved by us.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence **"We love Nathan"** is in the **active voice.**
 
• To convert it into the passive voice, the object of the active sentence (Nathan) becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The verb** "love"** changes to **"is loved"** to match the subject** "Nathan."**
 
• The subject of the active sentence (we) becomes the agent in the passive sentence and is preceded by **"by."**
 
• Therefore, the correct sentence in the passive voice is **"Nathan is loved by us."**

**Correct Sentence:** ***"Nathan is loved by us."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Nathan is being loved by us." - This is incorrect because "is being loved" implies a continuous action, which is not needed here.
 
• **Option 3:** "Nathan has been loved by us." - This is incorrect because "has been loved" implies a perfect tense, which is not needed here.
 
• **Option 4:** "Nathan have been loved by us." - This is incorrect due to the grammatical error "have been" instead of "has been."

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

A Mercedes-Benz was owned by my father.

options.text: My father has been owning a Mercedes-Benz.
My father has owned a Mercedes-Benz.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence given is in the** passive voice.**
 
• To convert it to **active voice, **the subject should perform the action directly.
 
• In the active voice,** "My father"** becomes the subject who performed the action of owning.
 
• Thus, the correct active voice sentence is **"My father owned a Mercedes-Benz."**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

**Correct Sentence:** *"My father owned a Mercedes-Benz."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "My father has been owning a Mercedes-Benz."** – This option is incorrect because "has been owning" is not a standard English construction.
 
• **Option 2: "My father owns a Mercedes-Benz."** – This option is incorrect because it changes the tense of the original sentence.
 
• **Option 3: "My father has owned a Mercedes-Benz."** – This option is incorrect because it changes the tense and aspect of the original sentence.
 
• **Option 4: "My father owned a Mercedes-Benz."** – This option correctly converts the sentence to active voice while maintaining the original tense.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

He said, “She has finished the painting.”

options.text: He said she has finished the painting.
He said that she had finished the painting.
He said she had finished the painting.
She has finished the painting he said.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In indirect speech, the** present perfect tense** is usually changed to the **past perfect tense.**
 
• The direct speech sentence **"She has finished the painting." **is in the present perfect tense.
 
• When converted to indirect speech, **"has finished"** changes to** "had finished."**
 
• The conjunction** "that"** is often used to introduce the reported speech.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** He said she has finished the painting. – This option incorrectly keeps the present perfect tense, which should change in indirect speech.
 
• **Option 3:** He said she had finished the painting. – This option is partially correct but omits the conjunction "that."
 
• **Option 4:** She has finished the painting he said. – This option incorrectly places the reported speech at the beginning and needs proper structuring.

questions.question: Identify the most suitable inference from the given passage.

options.text: Colds are minor infections of the nose and throat caused by viruses. Rhinovirus is the most common cause of common cold.
Medical Science has not yet resolved the problem of the common cold. Therefore, we have to suffer colds for some more time.
When your immune system is exposed to a new germ for the first time, it responds by trying to fight it off.
The viruses causing cold attack only on the surface and become immune to it.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Explanation:** The passage **explains** the challenges medical science faces in solving the problem of the common cold, despite advances in other areas such as transplant surgery and eradicating diseases like** Typhus and the Plague.**
 
• It** highlights** the difficulties posed by the variety of viruses causing colds and the technical challenges in studying these viruses.
 
• The conclusion that we will have to suffer colds for some **time** yet is made clear at the end of the passage.
 
• **In summary, option 2 best represents the main inference from the passage, emphasizing the ongoing struggle of medical science to solve the problem of the common cold and the implication that we will continue to suffer from colds for the foreseeable future.** Options 1, 3, and 4 either provide factual information or contain inaccuracies that do not capture the core inference of the passage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Colds are minor infections of the nose and throat caused by viruses. Rhinovirus is the most common cause of common cold:** While this statement is true and mentioned in the passage, it is more of a factual summary rather than an inference drawn from the passage.
 
• **When your immune system is exposed to a new germ for the first time, it responds by trying to fight it off:** This is a general statement about the immune response and is not the main inference to be drawn from the passage.
 
• **The viruses causing cold attack only on the surface and become immune to it:** This statement is incorrect as it misrepresents the function and behavior of cold viruses. The passage does not discuss viruses becoming immune to anything.
 
• In **summary**, **option 2** best represents the main inference from the passage, emphasizing the ongoing struggle of medical science to solve the problem of the common cold and the implication that we will continue to suffer from colds for the foreseeable future. **Options 1, 3, and 4** either provide factual information or contain inaccuracies that do not capture the core inference of the passage.

questions.question: Medical science has not done anything yet to solve the problem of the common cold because:

options.text: we can control one of the commonest of all diseases
viruses are so much smaller than the bacteria that cause many other infections; they cannot be seen with ordinary microscopes
other viruses get into the bloodstream where anti-bodies oppose them
bacteria causes many common infections such as pneumonia, wound infections and bloodstream infections

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Options 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Explanation:** The passage **explains** several reasons why medical science has not yet solved the problem of the common cold.
 
• **One key reason is that viruses are much smaller than bacteria and cannot be seen with ordinary microscopes, making them difficult to study.**
 
• This** technical challenge, **along with the fact that viruses cannot be easily cultivated in laboratories, greatly complicates the research and development of cures or vaccines for the common cold.
 
• **In summary, option 2 is the most accurate answer as it highlights the technical difficulties in studying viruses, which is a significant reason why medical science has not yet solved the problem of the common cold.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **We can control one of the commonest of all diseases:** This is incorrect because the passage specifically discusses the difficulty in controlling the common cold, not that we have control over it.
 
• **Other viruses get into the bloodstream where anti-bodies oppose them:** While this is true for some viruses, the statement does not directly address the specific problem of studying and combating cold viruses as mentioned in the passage. Additionally, cold viruses typically infect the lining of the nose and respiratory passages, not directly entering the bloodstream.
 
• **Bacteria cause many common infections such as pneumonia, wound infections, and bloodstream infections:** This statement is true in a general sense but does not explain why the common cold, which is caused by viruses, remains a problem despite advances in medical science. The comparison to bacteria-caused infections is not pertinent to the passage's main point.
 
• In **summary**, **option 2** is the most accurate answer as it highlights the technical difficulties in studying viruses, which is a significant reason why medical science has not yet solved the problem of the common cold.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate summary of the given passage?

options.text: The problem of common cold is unusually difficult, hence, we are likely to get relief from cold.
Virus research has led to the discovery of a large number of viruses and leaves the victim immune to further attacks.
Usually, a bacteria strikes only once and we do not gain immunity from colds
In spite of having the cure to kill diseases like Typhus and Plague, it seems ridiculous that medical science has not done much yet to solve the problem of the common cold.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Explanation:** The passage** expresses **frustration over the fact that while medical science has achieved significant milestones, such as performing transplant surgeries and eradicating fatal diseases like Typhus and the Plague,** it has not yet found a solution to the common cold.**
 
• This **resonates** with **option 4,** which **highlights** the contrast between advanced medical achievements and the persistent problem of the common cold.
 
• In summary, option 4 best captures the essence of the passage, highlighting the irony and ongoing challenge of dealing with the common cold despite medical advancements in treating other severe diseases. ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The problem of the common cold is unusually difficult, hence, we are likely to get relief from cold:** This option is incorrect because the passage does not suggest that we are likely to get relief from colds; rather, it emphasizes the persistence and difficulty of solving this problem.
 
• **Virus research has led to the discovery of a large number of viruses and leaves the victim immune to further attacks:** This option is incorrect because the passage states that we do not gain immunity from colds, which means we can catch them repeatedly.
 
• **Usually, a bacteria strikes only once and we do not gain immunity from colds:** This option is incorrect because the passage discusses viruses, not bacteria, in relation to colds and focuses on the lack of immunity from viral colds.
